sections.heading: Class tools start off
sections.lead: Swing and shot timers, Blessings and Totems are yours to turn on.
lines: Every class tool starts switched off: turn on the ones you want in Settings > Class tools.
After this update they are all off once, even ones you had on: switch yours back on.
Demo mode still shows every tool to try them out.

sections.heading: Smoother logins
lines: Opening the window no longer asks the game for a whole raid's items in the background.
A council member whose guild list loads late now answers everyone who logged in with them.

sections.heading: Recruitment
sections.lead: Guild > Recruitment: the people you talk to about joining, for the GM and officers.
lines: Add someone from a name's right-click menu, from Raids > Guests, or by name.
What they want, their spec, the nights they can raid and their own words.
Fits a team: their nights beside each team's raid nights, and an open place.
Every officer's notes in one story, with their guest raids and milestones.
Follow-ups remind you when they're online: they go on your friends list.
Pass someone to another officer; introductions nobody took remind everyone.
Bring them along: a group invite, a guest seat in a raid, or a member.
Invite: a welcome in guild chat, the officer note, the team's bench, its leaders told.
Then check-ins after a week and a month, level 58 and 70, first raid, gone quiet.
Message: build it from your words + helpers (classes a team needs, its nights).
Post to any channel, Say or Yell, each every 30 s or more; a key posts what is due.
Raids > Guests: Recruit now puts the guest in Recruitment (one list, not two).
Every member can introduce a friend from Guild > Members.
The Guild Master sets it up in Settings > Guild > Recruitment.

sections.heading: Walking together in 3D
sections.lead: The others walking in a strategy's room stay where they really are, as themselves.
lines: No more snapping: they run down the steps and stop at walls just as they really do.
Turns, strafing, backing off and jumps show as they happen.
Positions never wait in a queue, so what you see is never seconds old.
Their own race, sex and gear (helm and cloak only when shown).
/dz 3d looks npc: walkers of the other sex as a dressed NPC of their race.
A whole raid can walk together: 25 stay smooth, only the nearest hide behind pillars.
Walking and turning cost far less: a touch coarser while you move, sharp when you stop.

sections.heading: Swing timer (Warriors)
sections.lead: The swing timer's ring for Arms and Fury: both hands and your rage.
lines: The main hand on the outer ring, the off hand on an inner ring (gone with a two-hander).
Rage as a globe in the middle; Slate, Pips and Classic show it as a third bar.
A Heroic Strike lamp where the swing lands: pulsing = queue it, gold = queued.
The gold line on your rage: queue over it. 40 rage, or 80 for Arms with a two-hander.
Next presses from WoWSims: Bloodthirst, Whirlwind, Mortal Strike, Slam after the swing.
Only what you have: known spells, your stance, Execute under 20%, Rampage when usable.
Every timer theme; Settings > Class tools > Swing timer, /dz war, and demo mode.

sections.heading: A new Atlas
sections.lead: The Atlas is one wide page under a path you click: era, category, place, boss.
lines: Each part of the path is a menu: any raid by phase, any boss by its portrait.
Your recent places sit at the top of that menu, Classic and Heroic ones too.
A raid or dungeon opens on all its loot, one section per boss.
Loot shows as tiles; chips filter weapons, armor, jewelry and tokens.
Search finds places and bosses as well as items, in both eras: try "scar".
Up, Down and Enter walk the results; Shift+Enter adds an item to your BiS list.
Ctrl+F jumps to the search. Click a category's name to see its places as pictures.

sections.heading: Shopping list, by crafter
sections.lead: The shopping list has its own page behind the bag at the Atlas's top right.
lines: One card per crafter, online first, each with its own Whisper button.
The materials sit beside the cards, with the auction house total under them.
+ List on a craft adds it, says who can make it and offers Undo.

sections.heading: Atlas: Classic too
sections.lead: Classic or TBC as the first step of the Atlas's path, for level 1-60 characters.
lines: Classic: Molten Core to Ahn'Qiraj, every old dungeon, professions, factions and sets.
Dungeons are listed in level order, each with its levels beside it.
Below level 58 the Atlas opens on Classic, at the dungeon for your level.
Each side keeps where you were; a search says how many matches the other side has.

sections.heading: Game posters, easier to read
sections.lead: The Games posters say what's yours at a glance.
lines: The label over the painting sits on a dark pill, so it reads on any art.
Your numbers stand out: big figures with a small label under each.
Raid Trainer's times say they are best clears, and mark the boss you played last.
PLAY at the foot of the front poster; side posters keep just your one number.
Between raids Bingo shows your last card faded, with its lines.

sections.heading: A logo for every game
sections.lead: Bingo, Raid Trainer, Chess and Illidan have their own logos, like Azeromon.
lines: The logos stand in for the names on the Games posters.
Illidan's title screen and the Chess lobby open with theirs.
Bingo's logo stands over the card until a game deals you one.
Raid Trainer's briefing card carries it above the boss's name.

changelog.title: Recruitment, a Warrior swing timer and walking together

sections.heading: Groups
sections.lead: The Dungeons tab is now Groups: dungeons, raids, quests and PvP on one board.
lines: Tabs for every kind, each with how many groups it holds.
The groups that want you come first; the ones you can't join sink to the bottom.
Click a card to open it: who's in by role, the loot and bosses, why you fit.
Up to 10 players as seats, with your own portrait waiting in your place.
Bigger groups as raid frames, all 25 names in their class colours.
I'm up for: pick the kinds you want a ping for, dungeons and raids at first.
Raid lockouts count: a raid you're saved to says so and can't be joined.

lines.text: Raids on the board with dungeons, and the tab renamed Groups.

sections.heading: LFG message
sections.lead: Your group's LookingForGroup message, built from blocks and posted again every 30 s.

lines.text: What you need from your open places: damage split into melee and ranged, plus specs.
Blocks you click on or off and drag into order: name, 18/25, needs, when, loot, /w me.

lines: The exact text shows as you build it, counted against the channel's 255.

lines.text: Post again every 30 s to 2 min: a small poster lights up, one click or a key sends it.

lines: It stops by itself once the group is full.

sections.heading: List a group
sections.lead: One sheet for every kind, with the preview the guild sees.
lines: Raids as art tiles: a few of one size make one night; saved and locked ones are marked.
Places per role, full clear or picked bosses, rolls / soft reserve / loot council.
Other: attunements, world bosses, farming, reputation, or anything in the note.

sections.heading: Raid groups
sections.lead: Fill 25 places without a spreadsheet: your group gets its own page.
lines: The roster by role with the open places, what the group still lacks, the role meters.
Requests say what matters: BiS here, a buff you still lack, a blacklist warning, guests.
Guildies up for raids who fit an open place sit beside them with Invite.
Your BiS in a raid shows on its card; a missing attunement is a hint, never a block.
Arrive in the raid and a pop-up starts the raid session with your group's loot.
Planned raids short of players: Fill open places puts them on the board, with the team.
Joining a group that clashes with a raid you signed up for asks you first.

sections.heading: Quest groups
sections.lead: 220 group quests, starting from your own quest log.
lines: Your log first, then the quests guildies have, every zone with its own art, and a search.
Tick several quests in one zone: one group for all of them.
A quest that already has a group shows it with Join instead, so nobody lists it twice.
Pings go to guildies with the quest in their log; the group ends once you've turned it in.

sections.heading: PvP groups
sections.lead: Arenas, battlegrounds and world PvP, each with its own rules.
lines: Arena: the bracket, skirmish or rated (your team's, with a lowest rating for pings).
Someone who joins a rated group gets a team invite from you first.
Battleground premades sized to the battleground, with a flag carrier wanted.
PvP has no tanks: healers and damage only.

sections.heading: UI profiles
sections.lead: Looks, layout and key binds in one profile, and one per spec.
lines: Settings > Profiles: every profile as a card, with what it holds and its specs.
Each profile holds looks, layout and key binds; switch off a part to leave it alone.
Give a spec its profile: a respec switches your whole UI by itself.
Give a profile to any of your characters: your main and your alts each wear their own.
Looks that replace frames ask for a reload; in a fight the switch waits for its end.
What you change while a profile is in use saves into it.
Share sends the whole profile; you pick which parts to use before you switch.
Edit layout and Key binds show the profile they save into, with a menu to switch.

sections.heading: Vendor visits
sections.lead: Junk sells and your gear mends as soon as you talk to a vendor.

lines.text: Settings > Looks > Bags: sell junk and repair, each its own switch, off by default.
Pick how far up it sells on a rarity ladder: junk only, or up to common or uncommon gear.

lines: Above grey only weapons and armour sell, soulbound ones unless you say otherwise.
Gear in an outfit or on your BiS lists never sells; Check my bags shows what would.

lines.text: Repairs come from your own gold, never the guild bank; chat says what it cost.

lines: Works with the game's own bags too.

sections.heading: New ranks onto your bars
sections.lead: Learn a new rank and it takes the old one's place on your action bars.

lines.text: A new rank replaces the old one on your bars as soon as you learn it.

lines: Every bar and page, stance and form bars too; macros are left alone.
Only your best rank moves up: a lower rank kept for down-ranking stays.
In combat it waits for the fight to end.
On by default: Settings > Looks > Action bars, New ranks onto the bars.

sections.heading: Key binds
sections.lead: Point at any action button and press a key: its key, right there.
lines: Every button shows its key as a small cap; the one under the mouse lights up and listens.
Modifiers, the mouse wheel and the side mouse buttons all bind.
A key taken from another button moves, and a note says where it came from.
Right-click or Esc on a button clears it; undo, redo, and Discard puts every key back.
Drag an ability onto another to swap them.
For this character only, or the whole account.
Opens from the Esc menu, /dz keys, a minimap pin, a key binding or Settings.

sections.heading: Aggro warning
sections.lead: Unit, party and raid frames light up as someone nears pulling aggro off the tank.

lines.text: An outline that slides from yellow to red as their threat climbs toward the pull.

lines: A soft glow round it; from amber on it breathes, faster as they get close.
Someone who has pulled throbs deep red. Tanks never light up.
Off by default: Settings > Looks, Unit frames or Party and raid; it starts at 50-90%.
Demo mode and Edit layout show it on the made-up members.

sections.heading: Errors in bug reports
sections.lead: A bug report can carry the whole error, pasted from BugSack.

lines.text: Something broke: Paste error puts the error in its own window, apart from your words.

lines: A report with an error has a red warning icon in its header: click it to read and copy it.

sections.heading: Fixes
lines: Fixed: the game's Quick Keybind Mode no longer errors when you drop an ability.

lines.text: Fixed: nameplates only show Execute or Hammer of Wrath at 20% once you've learned it.

changelog.title: Groups, UI profiles and key binds

sections.heading: Azeromon: Blackrock
sections.lead: A new region north of Darkshire, from Redridge to Blackrock Mountain.
lines: Lakeshire, Stonewatch Keep, the Burning Steppes, the Searing Gorge and the Imperial Seat.
36 new beasts, 12 new moves, badges 6 and 7; Nefarius is your rival, twice.
Tame Magmadar once in the Molten Core; a Dark Iron Bar evolves a Harvest Watcher.
Professions go to 175, Dark Iron needs the Black Forge; beasts drop materials.
A painted world map with mist over places you haven't found yet.
A new pixel font, cream windows and a sun or moon for the time of day.

sections.heading: Gems for the hit cap
sections.lead: Suggested gems now know whether your gear is hit capped.
lines: Under the cap, Suggest adds hit gems where they cost least, up to the cap.
Already capped: no hit gems. Your meta gem stays active either way.
Counts your gear, enchants, talents, race and the Gear sim's buffs (dps specs it covers).

sections.heading: Fixes

lines.text: Wardrobe: an outfit's items show their enchant and gems in the tooltip.

lines: 3D strategy walks: others wear their race's clothes, not a white body.
Walking together: others run and turn smoothly, without jumping to and fro.
Square minimap: addon buttons, mail and queue icons sit on its edge, not on a circle.
Minimap: a long zone name is cut short before the clock instead of running under it.
Bank: buying a bank bag slot works again.
Bags: the bag slots in the footer equip and take off bags; round ringed slots in Halo.
Bars: the game's latency bar is hidden while a look is on.
Cast bars: learning a recipe shows the recipe's icon, not the game's placeholder face.
Azeromon: a move's info window shows again in the fight menu.

sections.heading: Discord without a host
sections.lead: The guild's Discord bot runs on its own server now, always on.
lines: Link your launcher once: /launcher in Discord, then paste the code in Settings > Discord.
After every save (login, /reload, logout) your game's raids and lists reach Discord.
Changes made in Discord reach the game when anyone linked logs in or reloads.
The first game to load them passes them on to everyone online.
Every change from Discord is signed by the bot: the game checks it and ignores fakes.
Guests from Discord wait for a raid leader; lists of non-addon players, for the council.

sections.heading: The launcher
sections.lead: Launcher 0.3.0 updates itself; it has a new Settings > Discord.
lines: Settings > Discord: link, sync now, unlink, and when it last synced.
It asks the bot only while WoW runs, so it stays quiet the rest of the time.
Host mode is gone: nobody's PC has to run the bot any more.
